videos.name: Y Combinator
videos.title: Building the AI Platform for Enterprise Software Implementations
videos.description:
Auctor (YC P25) is building an AI platform for enterprise software implementations, connecting business requirements to design, configuration, and go-live on platforms like Salesforce, ServiceNow, and SAP. The company recently closed a Series A from Sequoia.

In this episode of Founder Firesides, Auctor’s founders sit down with YC’s Pete Koomen to share how a photo with their dog brought in hundreds of demos—and why building for those demos left them with a product customers struggled to adopt. They discuss the roughly two-month rewrite that drove usage up 5–10x, the customer trust that made it possible, and why solving customers’ problems isn’t the same as building every feature they ask for. They also explain why AI could strengthen enterprise software rather than replace it.

https://getauctor.com

Chapters:
00:00 — AI for Enterprise Software Implementations
03:28 — Finding the Real Problem to Solve
06:46 — The Dog Photo That Booked Hundreds of Demos
10:13 — When Building for Demos Backfires
13:59 — The Rewrite That Increased Usage 5–10x
18:09 — Why Customers Stayed Through the Rebuild
22:17 — Why Enterprises Still Need Salesforce and SAP
26:21 — Building on Platforms, Not Replacing Them

videos.name: Latent Space
videos.title: Building Visual Intelligence — Andreas Blattmann & Dustin Podell, Black Forest Labs
videos.description:
A camera moves around a person. Halfway around, the model has to draw the back of a head it has never seen. How much can it learn about that missing view just by watching video? That’s the question we put to Andreas Blattmann and Dustin Podell of Black Forest Labs.

Their answer runs through FLUX 3. BFL trained one backbone on images, video and audio. The guests explain what each adds, how they decide which parts of denoising deserve the most compute, and why a detail that looks great in a still can flicker from frame to frame. We also get into the case for autoregression and where they think diffusion still has an edge.

There’s personal history here. Stable Diffusion is why Dustin left his software job and why swyx started Latent Space. They revisit the first FLUX training run in a French chalet, the photo experiment behind FLUX Kontext, and some of the things people actually use these models for, from restoring old family photos to generating a clip with synchronized sound.

This episode is sponsored by Deepgram. Deepgram is the voice AI infrastructure behind natural conversation—bringing speech-to-text, text-to-speech, voice-focused LLMs, and agents to teams building with voice AI. https://deepgram.com/?utm_source=latent-space&utm_medium=sponsored-podcast&utm_campaign=fy26_q4_brand_campaign&utm_term=latent-space&utm_content=host-read-youtube
